description.value: A within-subject fMRI cue-reactivity study tested how cigarette availability and transient DLPFC inactivation affect craving-related brain activity and functional connectivity in moderate-to-heavy smokers.

spans.text: The fMRI study comprised a within-subject 2 × 2 factorial design with factors of “cigarette availability” and “TMS,”

value: We hypothesized that the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) regulates craving during changes in intertemporal availability.
We also hypothesized that information regarding the immediacy of drug availability may be processed in circuitry including the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC).

spans.text: We hypothesize that cue-induced craving is a reflection of the current net value of the drug for the addicted individual, as a function of drug cues and drug-related context, and may be encoded in the medial orbitofrontal cortex (mOFC).

description.value: Within-subject 2 × 2 factorial design with cigarette availability and TMS, across four sessions on different days; session order was randomized and counterbalanced.

value: The BOLD signal in the mOFC displayed a higher correlation with craving in the immediate availability condition than the delayed condition during sham TMS sessions, but this difference was reduced by true TMS.
These data suggest that craving-correlated signals normally processed by the mOFC are amenable to modulation by inputs from the DLPFC that carry information on cigarette availability.

TMS and availability interactively altered functional connectivity
Finally, we performed a psychophysiological interaction analysis to measure DLPFC functional connectivity while participants watched the smoking video.

value: TMS and availability interactively altered functional connectivity of the DLPFC with the mOFC and the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex.

Functional connectivity with the left DLPFC was greater during the immediate compared with the delayed availability condition, and this effect was reduced by TMS; in the ventral striatum, functional connectivity was reduced during immediate compared with delayed availability during sham TMS, with the effect again reduced by TMS.
